questions.prompt: Patter reads the line aloud: "I'm fine." Cal's voice register says quiet, low, careful. Which playback choice carries the most of Cal's register?

options.label: A slower rate, a slightly lower pitch, and a small pause at the end.
A faster, brighter delivery so the line sounds cheerful.
A flat monotone with no pauses.

questions.mentorPostScript: Rest says: a slower pace + a pause is how 'I'm fine' becomes 'I am very much not fine.'

questions.prompt: Iris's voice register is fast, bright, lilting. Patter is queueing the read-aloud playback. Which two register words most affect the rate + pitch?

options.label: Fast → higher rate. Bright → higher pitch.
Fast → lower pitch. Bright → slower rate.

questions.mentorPostScript: Glance grins: the register word IS the playback recipe. Fast + bright = quick + lift.

questions.prompt: When you press 'Listen' on a tree with two characters, what's the most useful thing to listen for?

options.label: Whether the two characters sound like different people when their voices land back-to-back.
Whether the playback finishes faster than reading silently.
Whether every word is pronounced perfectly.

questions.mentorPostScript: Two voices, side by side, is the test. If they blur, the register did the blurring.

questions.prompt: Sprig says: every action beat in the tree gets a small pause on either side when Patter reads it aloud. Why?

options.label: An action beat is silence — the body doing something. The pause lets the listener feel it.
The playback engine can't pronounce action beats.
Action beats are louder than dialogue and need a buffer.

questions.mentorPostScript: The pause IS the beat. The listener hears the body.

questions.prompt: After the read-aloud finishes, what's the most useful next thing to do?

options.label: Rewrite any line where the voice felt wrong for that character — the ear caught what the eye missed.
Publish the tree immediately so the audio file doesn't go to waste.
Change every character's voice register to match the playback voice.

questions.mentorPostScript: Listening is a revision tool. What sounded wrong IS wrong.
